'''Diego López Rodríguez''' ({{IPA|es|ˈdjeɣo ˈlopeθ}}; born 3 November 1981) is a Spanish former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]].

After spending seven years with [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], playing for its various teams, he made a name for himself in [[La Liga]] with [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]], appearing in 230 official games over the course of five seasons. In 2013, following a brief spell with [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]], he returned to Real Madrid.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2021/11/02/primera/1635882282_169406.html|title=Diego López: 40 años, 40 paradas|trans-title=Diego López: 40 years, 40 saves|newspaper=[[Diario AS]]|first=Iván|last=Molero|language=es|date=3 November 2021|access-date=2 January 2024}}</ref>

López represented [[Spain national football team|Spain]] at the [[2009 FIFA Confederations Cup|2009 Confederations Cup]].

==Club career==
===Real Madrid===
López was born in [[Paradela, Lugo]], [[Galicia (Spain)|Galicia]]. A youth graduate from hometown's [[CD Lugo]] he signed with [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] at age 18 and, after a loan at another side from [[Community of Madrid|the capital region]], [[AD Alcorcón]], he eventually moved up to [[Real Madrid Castilla|Real's B team]], starting in his [[2004–05 Segunda División B|second season]], which ended in promotion to the [[Segunda División]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vavel.com/es/futbol/2018/03/06/espanyol/888359-diego-lopez-el-gallego-que-freno-a-leo-messi.html|title=Diego López, el gallego que frenó a Leo Messi|trans-title=Diego López, the Galician who stopped Leo Messi|publisher=Vavel|first=Pedro|last=Armas González|language=es|date=6 March 2018|access-date=1 February 2021}}</ref>

López served as first-team backup to [[Iker Casillas]] in the following two [[La Liga]] campaigns: in the closing stages of [[2005–06 La Liga|2005–06]] he appeared in back-to-back away wins, against [[CA Osasuna]] (as Casillas was [[Ejection (sports)|sent off]])<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=188635&cc=5739|title=Osasuna 0–1 Real Madrid|publisher=[[ESPN FC|ESPN Soccernet]]|date=30 April 2006|access-date=17 May 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121025001743/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=188635&cc=5739|archive-date=25 October 2012}}</ref> and [[Racing de Santander]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=188379&cc=5739|title=Racing Santander 2–3 Real Madrid|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=4 May 2006|access-date=17 May 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121025001749/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=188379&cc=5739|archive-date=25 October 2012}}</ref> adding a [[UEFA Champions League]] group stage game at [[Olympiacos F.C.|Olympiakos FC]], a [[2005–06 UEFA Champions League|2–1 defeat]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=188827&cc=5739|title=Olympiakos 2–1 Real Madrid: Second-string|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=6 December 2005|access-date=17 May 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121025001802/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=188827&cc=5739|archive-date=25 October 2012}}</ref>

===Villarreal===
[[File:Diego Lopez autograph signing, Wigan Athletic v Villarreal CF, 7 August 2011.jpg|thumb|left|López signing autographs with [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]] in 2011]]
In late June 2007, López signed with [[Villarreal CF]] for a reported fee of [[Euro|€]]6 million,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/news-media/news/01c2-0f84b22477b6-d7c56783e735-1000--diego-lopez-signs-at-villarreal/|title=Diego López signs at Villarreal|publisher=UEFA|date=26 June 2007|access-date=22 March 2025}}</ref> and started [[2007–08 La Liga|the season]] as second choice to Uruguayan [[Sebastián Viera]] but, after a string of fine performances – he played in the [[Copa del Rey]] and the [[2007–08 UEFA Cup|UEFA Cup]] – he was picked for the first team, finishing the season with 21 matches.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://futbol.as.com/futbol/2008/05/02/mas_futbol/1209709609_850215.html|title=Diego López, a superar los récords de Pepe Reina|trans-title=Diego López, chasing Pepe Reina's records|newspaper=Diario AS|first=Arnau|last=Andrés|language=es|date=2 May 2008|access-date=15 June 2016}}</ref>

López was ever-present in [[2008–09 La Liga|2008–09]], playing every minute and helping Villarreal finish fifth in the league. [[2009–10 La Liga|The following campaign]] was similar,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://es.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/01f0-0ea22dee396f-f69a10f574a8-1000--el-jugador-incombustible-del-villarreal/|title=El jugador incombustible del Villarreal|trans-title=Villarreal's tireless player|publisher=UEFA|first=Paul|last=Bryan|language=es|date=5 April 2011|access-date=15 June 2016}}</ref> but the team could only finish seventh, out of the European places. However, as fifth-placed [[RCD Mallorca]] were expelled from European competition due to bankruptcy, the [[Valencian Community|Valencians]] took their place in the [[2010–11 UEFA Europa League|qualifying rounds]] of the [[UEFA Europa League]].

López featured in every league game except one in [[2011–12 La Liga|2011–12]], being given his marching orders against [[Sevilla FC]] in a 2–2 home draw in the second round.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/324010?cc=5739|title=Villarreal claim battling draw|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=10 September 2011|access-date=24 May 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121102085423/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/324010?cc=5739|archive-date=2 November 2012}}</ref> The ''Yellow Submarine'' were eventually relegated after twelve years, with the player conceding 50 goals. His 121 consecutive top-flight games set a 21st-century record in the league, which was broken by [[Iñaki Williams]] in 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://eldesmarque.com/bizkaia/athletic-club/222127-williams-hace-historia-en-laliga|title=Williams hace historia en LaLiga|trans-title=Williams makes history in LaLiga|publisher=El Desmarque|language=es|date=30 August 2019|access-date=21 January 2021}}</ref>

===Sevilla===
On 22 May 2012, López joined Sevilla on a five-year contract for a reported fee of €3.5 million.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sevillafc.es/nuevaweb/actualidad/noticias/24945/el-sevilla-ficha-a-diego-lopez-un-portero-de-altura-para-el-nuevo-proyecto|title=El Sevilla ficha a Diego López, un portero de altura para el nuevo proyecto|trans-title=Sevilla sign Diego López, tall goalkeeper for new project|publisher=Sevilla FC|language=es|date=22 May 2012|access-date=22 May 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120525093741/http://www.sevillafc.es/nuevaweb/actualidad/noticias/24945/el-sevilla-ficha-a-diego-lopez-un-portero-de-altura-para-el-nuevo-proyecto|archive-date=25 May 2012}}</ref> He split first-choice status with [[Andrés Palop]] during his spell.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sevilla.eldesmarque.com/sevilla-futbol-club/50315-palop-vs-diego-lopez-enesima-parte|title=Palop vs Diego López, enésima parte|trans-title=Palop vs Diego López, part umpteen|publisher=El Desmarque|first=Álvaro|last=Ramírez|language=es|date=18 January 2013|access-date=8 April 2016}}</ref>

===Return to Real Madrid===
[[File:Diego López real madrid.JPG|thumb|right|López in action for [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in 2013]]
On 25 January 2013, López returned to Real Madrid after Casillas suffered a hand injury which ruled him out for 12 weeks, signing for €3.5 million until June 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/es/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo/1330134913406/noticia/Noticia/Diego_Lopez,_nuevo_jugador_del_Real_Madrid.htm|title=Diego López, nuevo jugador del Real Madrid|trans-title=Diego López, new Real Madrid player|publisher=Real Madrid CF|language=es|date=25 January 2013|access-date=26 January 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130603031124/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/es/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo/1330134913406/noticia/Noticia/Diego_Lopez,_nuevo_jugador_del_Real_Madrid.htm|archive-date=3 June 2013}}</ref> Shortly upon arriving, he stated he had always dreamed of coming back to the club.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/es/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo/1330135006548/noticia/Entrevista/Diego_Lopez:_%E2%80%9CVolver_al_club_de_mi_corazon_es_algo_muy_especial%E2%80%9D.htm|title=Diego López: "Volver al club de mi corazón es algo muy especial"|trans-title=Diego López: "Returning to the club of my heart is quite special"|publisher=Real Madrid CF|language=es|date=26 January 2013|access-date=26 January 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130129071621/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/es/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo/1330135006548/noticia/Entrevista/Diego_Lopez:_%E2%80%9CVolver_al_club_de_mi_corazon_es_algo_muy_especial%E2%80%9D.htm|archive-date=29 January 2013}}</ref>

López played his first game in his second spell on 30 January 2013, in a 1–1 home draw against [[FC Barcelona]] in the [[2012–13 Copa del Rey|Spanish Cup semi-finals]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=360213&cc=5739|title=Varane keeps Real hopes alive|publisher=ESPN FC|date=30 January 2013|access-date=31 January 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130216032934/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=360213&cc=5739|archive-date=16 February 2013}}</ref> On 5 March, he made a string of saves as Real beat [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] 2–1 at [[Old Trafford]] to [[2012–13 UEFA Champions League|qualify for the last-eight in the Champions League]] (3–2 on aggregate); after the match, coach [[José Mourinho]] said: "Diego López was the best player in my team".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en-sg/news/3907/champions-league/2013/04/04/3876985/mourinho-cant-recall-casillas-with-diego-lopez-in-such-fantastic-|title=Mourinho can't recall Casillas with Diego Lopez in such fantastic form|publisher=[[Goal (website)|Goal]]|first=Ben|last=Hayward|date=4 April 2013|access-date=5 April 2013}}</ref> He retained his position until the end of [[2012–13 La Liga|the season]], even though Casillas had already returned to full fitness.

López retained his number one position at the start of [[2013–14 La Liga|the following campaign]], when [[Carlo Ancelotti]] had replaced Mourinho. Casillas was played in both the Champions League and the domestic cup, however.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.101greatgoals.com/blog/ancelottis-bizarre-solution-to-keeper-issue-lopez-plays-liga-casillas-plays-europe-marca/|title=Ancelotti's bizarre solution to keeper issue: Lopez plays Liga, Casillas plays Europe [Marca]|publisher=101 Great Goals|date=5 September 2013|access-date=8 September 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140316110437/http://www.101greatgoals.com/blog/ancelottis-bizarre-solution-to-keeper-issue-lopez-plays-liga-casillas-plays-europe-marca/|archive-date=16 March 2014}}</ref>

===AC Milan===
On 13 August 2014, Real Madrid and [[AC Milan]] reached an agreement over the transfer of López.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/08/official-statement-diego-lopez|title=Official statement: Diego López|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=13 August 2014|access-date=13 August 2014}}</ref> He made his competitive debut on 31 August in the first match of the [[2014–15 Serie A|new season]] in [[Serie A]], saving a late [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalty]] from [[Antonio Candreva]] in a 3–1 win over [[SS Lazio]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en-gb/match/milan-vs-lazio/1836107|title=AC Milan 3–1 Lazio: Inzaghi era starts with a bang|publisher=Goal|date=31 August 2014|access-date=31 August 2014}}</ref> On 14 September he suffered a right thigh injury against [[Parma Calcio 1913|Parma FC]], being sidelined for almost a month.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2199177-diego-lopez-injury-updates-on-ac-milan-stars-thigh-and-return|title=Diego Lopez injury: Updates on AC Milan star's thigh and return|publisher=[[Bleacher Report]]|first=Timothy|last=Rapp|date=15 September 2014|access-date=8 October 2014}}</ref>

After three matches without a win early into the [[2015–16 Serie A|2015–16 campaign]], manager [[Siniša Mihajlović]] dropped López in favour of 16-year-old [[Gianluigi Donnarumma]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34632553|title=European football: Neymar selfie, Pogba gets shirty|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=25 October 2015|access-date=25 October 2015}}</ref>

===Espanyol===
On 31 August 2016, López joined [[RCD Espanyol]] on a [[2016–17 La Liga|season]]-long loan deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.acmilan.com/en/news/first-team/2016-08-31/ac-milan-official-statement|title=AC Milan official statement|publisher=A.C. Milan|date=31 August 2016|access-date=31 August 2016}}</ref> He was elected [[La Liga Player of the Month]] in November, after not conceding in any of the three matches.<ref name=Month>{{cite web|url=http://www.laliga.es/en/news/diego-lopez-named-laliga-santander-player-of-the-month-for-november|title=Diego Lopez named LaLiga Santander Player of the Month for November|publisher=[[La Liga]]|date=16 December 2016|access-date=14 March 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180107174844/http://www.laliga.es/en/news/diego-lopez-named-laliga-santander-player-of-the-month-for-november|archive-date=7 January 2018}}</ref>

López's move was made permanent on 23 May 2017, on a three-year deal with a [[buyout clause]] of €50 million.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://sport.repubblica.it/news/sport/calcio-milan-ceduto-a-titolo-definitivo-diego-lopez-all-espanyol/4697070|title=Calcio, Milan: Ceduto a titolo definitivo Diego Lopez all'Espanyol|trans-title=Football, Milan: Diego Lopez transferred permanently to Espanyol|newspaper=[[La Repubblica]]|language=it|date=23 May 2017|access-date=2 June 2017}}</ref> He was overtaken by [[Pau López]] still under manager [[Quique Sánchez Flores]],<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/20171015/432092878416/pau-se-consolida-y-desafia-la-jerarquia-de-diego-lopez.html|title=Pau se consolida y desafía la jerarquía de Diego López|trans-title=Pau solidifies and defies Diego Lopez's hierarchy|newspaper=[[Mundo Deportivo]]|language=es|date=15 October 2017|access-date=18 January 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2017/12/30/primera/1514631316_470951.html|title=Pau y Diego: un 2018 con intercambio de papeles|trans-title=Pau and Diego: 2018 with a change of roles|newspaper=Diario AS|first=Alberto|last=Martínez|language=es|date=30 December 2017|access-date=18 January 2018}}</ref> but after the latter moved to [[Real Betis]], he regained his starting role and was the only player to feature in all 38 games of [[2018–19 La Liga|2018–19]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/rcd-espanyol/20190518/462309708375/espanyol-diego-lopez-pleno-partidos-completos.html|title=Diego López, único candidato al 'pleno al 38' |trans-title=Diego López, only candidate to the 'full 38'|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|first=Jaume|last=Miserachs|language=es|date=20 May 2019|access-date=21 January 2021}}</ref>

In August 2020, after Espanyol's relegation, the nearly 39-year-old López signed for [[2020–21 Segunda División|another season]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.lavozdegalicia.es/noticia/lugo/2020/08/18/portero-diego-lopez-renueva-espanyol-pese-descenso/0003_202008L18P289912.htm|title=El portero Diego López renueva con el Espanyol pese al descenso|trans-title=Goalkeeper Diego López renews with Espanyol despite relegation|newspaper=[[La Voz de Galicia]]|language=es|date=17 August 2020|access-date=21 January 2021}}</ref> In that year, he recorded the best figures for his position with 25 goals conceded in 40 matches, as the ''Pericos'' won the title.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/rcd-espanyol/20210531/494030258696/de-tomas-pichichi-y-diego-lopez-zamora.html|title=De Tomás, 'pichichi', y Diego López, 'Zamora'|trans-title=De Tomás, top scorer, and Diego López, best goalkeeper|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|first=Anna|last=Cordovilla|language=es|date=31 May 2021|access-date=2 June 2021}}</ref>

===Rayo Vallecano===
López signed a one-year contract with [[Rayo Vallecano]] on 2 July 2022, as a [[free agent]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/primera/diego-lopez-jugara-en-el-rayo-vallecano-la-proxima-temporada-n/|title=Diego López, segundo fichaje del Rayo de Iraola|trans-title=Diego López, second signing of Iraola's Rayo|newspaper=Diario AS|first=José Antonio|last=Zapico Díaz|language=es|date=2 July 2022|access-date=5 July 2022}}</ref> In December 2023, having been unemployed for six months, he announced his retirement aged 42.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tribalfootball.com/articles/ex-real-madrid-keeper-diego-lopez-announces-retirement-and-new-plans-4481025|title=Ex-Real Madrid keeper Diego Lopez announces retirement – and new plans|publisher=Tribal Football|first=Carlos|last=Volcano|date=28 December 2023|access-date=29 December 2023}}</ref>

==International career==
===Spain===
As third goalkeeper, López was first selected for [[Spain national football team|Spain]] for two [[2010 FIFA World Cup]] [[2010 FIFA World Cup qualification (UEFA)|qualifiers]] in late March/early April 2009, both against [[Turkey national football team|Turkey]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.elmundo.es/elmundodeporte/2009/03/20/futbol/1237548468.html|title=Diego López, la única novedad de Del Bosque|trans-title=Diego López, only Del Bosque novelty|newspaper=[[El Mundo (Spain)|El Mundo]]|language=es|date=20 March 2009|access-date=15 June 2016}}</ref> He was named in the squad by manager [[Vicente del Bosque]] for the [[2009 FIFA Confederations Cup]] in [[South Africa]] behind Casillas and [[Pepe Reina]], and did not play any matches there.<ref name=FCC>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2009/06/12/futbol/copa_confederaciones/espana/1244823325.html|title=Diego López: "Nueva Zelanda ya demostró contra Italia que tiene potencial"|trans-title=Diego López: "New Zealand have already shown against Italy they have potential"|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|language=es|date=12 June 2009|access-date=15 June 2016}}</ref>

López earned his only [[Cap (sport)|cap]] on 12 August 2009, playing the last 30 minutes of a 3–2 [[Exhibition game|friendly]] win against [[Macedonia national football team|Macedonia]], replacing Reina and not conceding any goals.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.europapress.es/deportes/futbol-00162/noticia-futbol-seleccion-cronica-macedonia-espana-20090812233357.html|title=Crónica del Macedonia-España: 2–3.|trans-title=Macedonia-Spain match report: 2–3.|publisher=[[Europa Press]]|language=es|date=12 August 2009|access-date=20 April 2014}}</ref>

===Galicia===
López made three appearances for the [[Galicia national football team|unofficial Galicia team]], starting with their first game for 75 years on 29 December 2005. They won 3–2 against [[Uruguay national football team|Uruguay]] in [[Santiago de Compostela]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/2005/12/30/pagina-22/748734/pdf.html#&mode=fullScreen|title=Histórico triunfo ante un bicampeón mundial|trans-title=Historic triumph against a two-time world champion|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|language=es|date=30 December 2005|access-date=20 August 2021}}</ref>

==Style of play==
López was a well-rounded goalkeeper, with a large physique, strong leadership qualities and good handling, which facilitated him in coming out to claim crosses. He possessed quick reactions, concentration and a positional sense, also being an effective shot-stopper.<ref name=GDS>{{cite news|url=http://www.gazzetta.it/Calciomercato/09-08-2014/milan-vecchi-diego-lopez-odia-prendere-gol-anche-allenamento-preparatore-portieri-inzaghi-9093386904.shtml|title=Milan, Vecchi su Diego Lopez: "Odia prendere gol, anche in allenamento"|trans-title=Milan, Vecchi on Diego Lopez: "He hates conceding goals, even in training"|newspaper=[[La Gazzetta dello Sport]]|first=Fabiana|last=Della Valle|language=it|date=10 August 2014|access-date=22 August 2016}}</ref><ref name=LR>{{cite news|url=http://www.repubblica.it/sport/calcio/fantacalcio/2014/08/19/news/inzaghi_blinda_i_pali_con_diego_lo_pez-94087275/|title=Inzaghi blinda i pali con Diego López|trans-title=Inzaghi shields the posts with Diego López|newspaper=La Repubblica|language=it|date=19 August 2014|access-date=22 August 2016}}</ref>

López was known in particular for his ball control, distribution and speed when [[Goalkeeper (association football)#Sweeper-keeper|rushing off his line]] to anticipate opponents.<ref name=GDS/><ref name=LR/>

==Personal life==
López married Iria Otero on 11 June 2011, fathering three children.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://playerwags.com/diego-lopezs-wife-iria-otero-rodriguez/|title=Diego Lopez's wife Iria Otero Rodriguez|publisher=Player Wags|date=2 August 2014|access-date=13 April 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150111155112/http://playerwags.com/diego-lopezs-wife-iria-otero-rodriguez/|archive-date=11 January 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://thepressportal.com/diego-lopez-and-iria-otero-will-be-parents-of-their-second-child-in-spring-of-2015/|title=Diego López and Iria Otero will be parents of their second child in spring of 2015|publisher=The Press Portal|first=John|last=Spartan|date=26 November 2014|access-date=13 April 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20150413205420/http://thepressportal.com/diego-lopez-and-iria-otero-will-be-parents-of-their-second-child-in-spring-of-2015/|archive-date=13 April 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/tikitakas/2018/04/25/portada/1524679847_490871.html|title=Diego López e Iria Otero dan la bienvenida a su tercera hija|trans-title=Diego López and Iria Otero welcome their third daughter|newspaper=Diario AS|first=Marcos|last=Méndez de la Peña|language=es|date=25 April 2018|access-date=27 April 2018}}</ref>
